title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide 2026
author: Alyssa Nguyen
body:
Summary:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s People Operations guidance for hiring, employee onboarding, ongoing performance and feedback cycles, and manager expectations. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, and new hires. Follow the steps below to ensure consistent candidate experience, fast time-to-hire, reliable onboarding outcomes, and fair performance programs across the company.

Scope and audience:
- Applies to all full-time and part-time hires, internal transfers, and contractor conversions unless a role-specific exception is documented.
- Primary readers: hiring managers, interview panelists, people-ops, recruiting operations, and engineering managers.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-offer to an average of <= 21 calendar days from requisition approval.
- Ensure 90% of new hires complete a 30/60/90 plan with their manager within the first 30 days.
- Maintain calibration and equitable performance ratings with structured rubric and training.

1) Hiring process (end-to-end):

Overview:
- We operate a centralized hiring workflow powered by Greenhouse (recruiting) and Lattice (performance), integrated with Okta for identity and GSuite and Slack for communication. The typical hiring journey is: requisition -> sourcing -> phone screen -> technical/cultural loop -> final onsite/virtual -> reference checks -> offer -> background check -> onboarding.

Steps and responsibilities:
1. Requisition & role definition (Hiring manager):
   - Submit a role requisition in Greenhouse with: title, level, team, hiring rationale, budget code, and JD template.
   - Attach a short 3–4 bullet priority list describing the top deliverables in the first 6 months.
   - People-ops reviews within 2 business days for headcount and compensation band alignment.

2. Sourcing & outreach (Recruiting):
   - Recruiters source passive candidates, post public role, and run outreach campaigns.
   - Hiring manager provides 3+ names for referrals and agrees an interview shortlist target within 5 business days.

3. Interview design and panel (Hiring manager + People-ops):
   - Use the standard interview loop templates (technical, behavioral, collaboration, role-specific) stored in the hiring playbook.
   - Interview panels must include at least one trained interviewer with diversity and inclusion interview certification.

4. Interviewing (Panel):
   - Use the standardized rubrics and scorecards in Greenhouse. Each interviewer submits scores within 48 hours.
   - Provide specific, observable evidence in the feedback; avoid vague statements like “good culture fit” without examples.

5. Debrief & decision (Hiring manager + Recruiter):
   - Recruiter coordinates a debrief within 48 hours of the final interview. Decision criteria: demonstrated skills, alignment to role priorities, team fit, and compensation.

6. Offer approval and compensation (People-ops + Finance):
   - Hiring manager requests offer approval in the compensation approval workflow with proposed base, equity range, and sign-on (if applicable).
   - People-ops and Finance route approvals within 3 business days for standard offers. Expedited path exists for candidate start dates <10 days.

7. Reference & background checks (Recruiting):
   - At least two professional references are verified for IC roles; leadership roles require at least three.
   - Background checks are initiated after offer acceptance and must be cleared before access is granted to sensitive systems.

8. Offer extension and closing (Recruiter):
   - Send a written offer letter with role, manager, start date, compensation breakdown, basic benefits summary, and background check contingency.
   - Follow up with a verbal call and candidate FAQ.

Hiring SLAs and metrics:
- Time-to-requisition approval: <= 2 business days.
- Time-to-phone-screen: <= 7 calendar days.
- Time-to-offer: target <= 21 calendar days (rolling quarterly metric).
- Offer acceptance rate target: >= 70%.

Templates and artifacts (links):
- Job description templates: /confluence/company-handbook/job-description-templates
- Interview rubrics and scorecards: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/interview-rubrics
- Offer letter templates: /confluence/company-handbook/offer-templates

2) Candidate experience & diversity best practices:
- Require at least one diverse candidate in every final slate for non-entry roles.
- Communicate frequently: recruiters update candidate status every 5 business days.
- Provide clear interview prep guidance and a single point of contact.

3) Pre-boarding and onboarding (first 90 days):

Pre-boarding (between offer acceptance and first day):
- People-ops checklist items (to complete before day 1):
  - Finalize start date, collect preboarding documents, create calendar invites for week 1, provision laptop order, create Okta user, grant initial Slack access and email alias, enroll in benefits (if eligible).
  - Manager actions: prepare 30/60/90 plan draft; set up 1:1 cadence; identify onboarding buddies; prepare role-specific decks.
  - IT & Security: ensure MDM profile, VPN access, and minimal set of service accounts exist.

First day agenda (example):
- Welcome + People Ops orientation (1 hour)
- Manager 1:1 (30 minutes) to review role, immediate priorities, and 30/60/90 plan
- Team welcome / lunch (30–60 minutes)
- System access & security walkthrough with IT (1 hour)

First week goals:
- Complete compliance and security training modules (IAM, data-handling basics)
- Complete access requests for required systems (Git, GCP/AWS, internal dashboards)
- Meet with cross-functional partners and product/infra owners relevant to role

30/60/90 plan expectations:
- 30 days: Understand core systems, key stakeholders, and deliverable ownership. Manager and new hire finalize and sign the plan.
- 60 days: Deliver first measurable contribution (bugfix, doc, small feature) and present learnings.
- 90 days: Lead a small project or own a repeatable operational task; manager completes an initial performance checkpoint.

Onboarding success metrics:
- 90% of new hires have an assigned buddy and completed 30/60/90 plan within 30 days.
- New hire happiness score >= 4/5 at 30-day survey.

4) Performance & feedback cycles:

Cadence and components:
- Ongoing feedback: Encourage weekly or biweekly manager 1:1s and ad hoc feedback for role adjustments.
- Formal cycles: Quarterly check-ins (light), mid-year review (semi-formal), and annual performance review (formal) tracked in Lattice.
- Calibration: People-ops facilitates a manager calibration process each review cycle to ensure consistency across teams.

Rating scale and rubric:
- Use the standardized 1–5 competency scale with narrative anchors and examples. Example anchors: 5 = consistently exceeds expectations across scope, demonstrates leadership and mentors others; 3 = meets expectations reliably; 1 = performance significantly below expectations.
- Competencies: job-specific delivery, collaboration & communication, impact & ownership, growth & learning, leadership (if applicable).

Manager responsibilities during reviews:
- Collect and document evidence: project outcomes, peer feedback, quantitative metrics.
- Prepare a written summary and development plan in Lattice.
- Discuss compensation and career path only after calibration and people-ops guidance.

Career ladders and leveling:
- Use published leveling guides stored in /confluence/eng-developer-experience/leveling.
- For promotions: managers propose promotion packets including work samples, impact statements, and peer endorsements. People-ops coordinates promotion committee review.

Performance improvement plans (PIPs):
- Initiate PIPs for employees with sustained performance below expectations after coaching.
- PIP timeline typically 60–90 days with clear success criteria, manager checkpoints every 2 weeks, and people-ops oversight.

Separation and offboarding:
- For voluntary exits, managers must submit offboarding requests to people-ops at least 2 weeks before last day.
- Offboarding tasks: revoke access, exit interview, knowledge transfer, final payroll coordination, equipment return.

5) Manager playbook (expectations & best practices):

Core responsibilities:
- Recruit and retain: partner with recruiting to hire strong teammates; make timely interview decisions and provide actionable feedback.
- Onboard effectively: own the 30/60/90 plan and ensure new hire has resources and context.
- Develop people: hold regular feedback conversations, build development plans, and advocate for promotions where merited.
- Run effective 1:1s: have an agenda, follow through on action items, and document outcomes.

Hiring-specific manager checklist (quick):
1. Define role priorities and success criteria.
2. Attend recruiter kickoff and provide interview panel & rubric.
3. Interview with structured scoring and timely feedback.
4. Make decision within 48 hours of final interview.
5. Complete onboarding 30/60/90 plan within first week.

Feedback and coaching:
- Follow a STAR feedback structure (Situation, Task, Action, Result).
- Document both strengths and areas to develop; provide actionable next steps and resources.

Manager training & resources:
- New manager onboarding course in LMS (required for people managers within 90 days of promotion/hire).
- Interviewer training and unconscious bias modules (required annually).
- People-ops office hours and playbook repository: /confluence/company-handbook/people-ops-playbook

6) Policies and exceptions:

Probation and confirmation:
- Standard probation: 90 days for new hires. For contractors converting to FTE, probation may be reduced to 30–60 days at manager discretion and people-ops approval.

Remote & hybrid work guidelines:
- Redwood supports flexible remote work. Teams define core collaboration hours; managers document team-specific expectations. See Remote Work Guidelines: /confluence/policies-and-process/remote-work-guidelines

Time off and leave:
- PTO accrual, paid parental leave, and short-term disability policies are in /confluence/company-handbook/time-off-and-leave. Consult people-ops for case-specific questions.

Compensation exceptions and equity grants:
- Special sign-on or equity exceptions require VP-level approval and Finance sign-off. Document rationale in the compensation approval workflow.

7) Metrics and reporting (people-ops):
- Monthly HR dashboard includes: headcount, open reqs, time-to-fill, offer acceptance rate, new hire retention (30/90-day), diversity metrics, ramp velocity, and manager satisfaction.
- Quarterly review with executive team for people planning and capacity.

8) Escalations and exceptions:
- Escalate hiring blockers (budget, approvals, background check failures) to people-ops lead.
- For performance disputes, follow this sequence: manager -> people-ops -> HRBP -> VP People. Formal appeals follow the dispute resolution policy.
